about: obis-hex URL -> the atlas URL of the same OBIS layer (build week 4, step 1). One table drives both sides: oceanmetrics/atlas tests/state/obisHex.test.ts (obisHexToAtlas) reads it here, and obis-hex copies it into tests/redirect.test.ts for its redirectFor. Each case: the obis-hex URL, the expected URL, whether the target shows what the old link showed (exact), and the obis-hex keys it does not carry (dropped; ?<key> for a query switch). Edit it here first, then copy.
notes: query keys are written in this order, encoded as the atlas's formatSel does (URLSearchParams: a space is +; then , : / unescaped); the hash pl is the p. token encoded the same way, so its % is %25
taxon splits on its first colon: the rank never holds one, the name may (an encoded colon in obis-hex's l)
dim.period also takes a year (2015) for the year layers of obis-h3 0.11; no obis-hex link names a year
the collection id is obis_h3 as the plan's grammar says; obisindicators' obis_h3_stac_collection() writes id obis-h3 today, so step 3 publishes it as obis_h3 or this table changes
the camera carries the same centre and zoom, but the atlas's panes cover other parts of the map, so the same camera is not the same view (not expressible)
?legacy= runs through obis-hex's legacyToState() before this table (no case here)

i.rule: es|sp|shannon|simpson|n, the same tokens; anything else is es

l.rule: all -> i=all; eov:<key> -> i=<key> (the item ids are all and the seven EOV keys); taxon:<rank>:<name> -> i=all&taxon=<rank>:<name> (split before decoding, as obis-hex); aphia:<id> -> i=all&taxon=aphia:<id>

p.rule: a decade 1960..2020 -> <decade>s; all, absent or anything else -> all; dropped to all for a taxon group (no taxon decades in the release)

r.rule: auto or 1..7, else auto; clamped to 5 with a decade, 5 for an aphia subtree, 4 for an aphia subtree with a decade

c.rule: obis-hex's camera lon,lat,zoom (read from the old hash only: the atlas's ?c= is the collection); malformed or absent -> the opening camera -103.7,33.2,2.57

g.rule: absent or globe -> proj=globe (written explicitly), flat -> proj=mercator

pl.rule: with l=all, i=es, p=all and r=auto -> /places/p/<id>; with any of them chosen -> the atlas, the place as the p. token (empty name) in the hash

pc.drop: the Place page is keyed by id and the p. token has no collection: the atlas resolves the id through the gazetteer index (inexact on the atlas side)

t.drop: obis-hex's theme, always written (default dark); the atlas's hash t is the report title, so it is never copied

o.drop: opacity: the atlas layer's own opacity control, not in the grammar

d.drop: ramp domain: the atlas legend's domain comes from stats.parquet (release p02 to p98)

k.drop: the open Controls tab: obis-hex layout

cc.drop: the Controls pane folded: obis-hex layout

tc.drop: the Time strip folded: obis-hex layout

x.drop: the selected hexagon: the grammar has no key for it yet (inexact)

xo.drop: the Cell pane open: follows x

f.drop: the place filter: the atlas place filter is H3 membership from the gazetteer, with no URL key yet; the Place page has the exact values (inexact)

v.drop: v=places, the view as places: replaced by the Place page (inexact)

?tour.rule: on|off, the atlas's own tour= switch

?theme.rule: dark|light, the atlas's own theme= switch

?modal.drop: the atlas has no switch that opens a Help modal

?data.drop: a pinned release base; the atlas's ?catalog= names a catalog, not a release (inexact)

?h3t.drop: the h3t service: the atlas makes no h3t request

?legacy.drop: a Shiny bookmark: obis-hex's legacyToState() turns it into a hash first (its redirect page runs it), then that hash follows this table; the atlas codec ignores the switch

cases.name: the default view
an EOV, Shannon, the 1990s (p=1990 is dim.period=1990s), res 3, obis-hex's rounded camera
seabirds, records, the 2020s, auto
p=all is the all-years value dim.period=all; a camelCase EOV key is the item id
a period that is not a decade (p=1995) is all years, as obis-hex reads it
r=7 with a decade is res 5, as obis-hex drew it
r=7 with all years stays 7
a resolution outside 1..7 (r=9) is auto, as obis-hex reads it
g=flat is proj=mercator
a link with only some keys: the missing camera is obis-hex's opening camera, the globe written
a malformed camera (two numbers) is the opening camera; an unknown indicator is es
the bare app, no hash
a taxon group: item all, taxon=<rank>:<name>
a taxon name with a space (encoded %20 in l): + in the atlas query
a taxon name with an encoded colon stays one name: taxon splits on its first colon
a raw colon in the name is four parts: obis-hex reads all taxa, so does the redirect
a taxon name with an encoded bar stays encoded (the grammar's | is an alternative, never a value)
a taxon group with a decade: the release has no taxon decades (obis-hex loaded nothing), the period is all
any WoRMS taxon: taxon=aphia:<id>, item all
aphia at r=7: the atlas serves a subtree up to res 5
aphia with a decade at r=5: the species table's decade variant is res 3 and 4
aphia on auto at zoom 9: obis-hex drew res 7, the atlas res 5
a place outlined and nothing else chosen: the Place page
a place id with a space and its collection: the Place page by id, pc dropped
a place on a chosen view: the atlas, the place as the p. token in the hash
a place with a space and its collection on a pinned resolution: the p. token, pc not carried
the selected hexagon and its open pane are dropped
the place filter and the view as places are dropped (the Place page has the exact values)
the layout keys and styling are dropped and the view stays exact
?tour and ?theme carry to the atlas's own tour= and theme=; the hash t never does
?modal and ?h3t are dropped
?data (a pinned release) is dropped: the atlas reads the current collection
